summary: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) was an Indology scholar. He studied at the East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and served as a professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter (1849–1894) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault and Michel Bréal, later holding posts there and at the Collège de France.

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock, and held a post at the University of Iowa as Professor Emeritus in 1971.
James Dwight Dana (1813–1895) studied at Yale College from ~1830 to 1833. He later held a post at Yale University from ~1850 to 1892, where he taught Charles Rockwell Lanman.
James Fergusson (1808–1886) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal High School and became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1840.

James Fieser (born 1958) works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Berea College (~1976–1980) and Purdue University (~1980–1986), and held posts at the University of Tennessee and the University of Tennessee at Martin around 1992.

James G. Mullens is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Simon Fraser University, the University of Victoria, and McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen, Yün-hua Jan, and John G. Arapura, holding a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James H. Austin (born 1925) is an academic neurologist active in Buddhist studies. He studied under Katsujo Terayama and Nanrei Sohaku Kobori, holding posts at the University of Oregon/OHSU, the University of Colorado, and the University of Idaho.

James Hadley (1821–1872) worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Fairfield Academy and Yale, where he studied under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, he taught at Middlebury College and served as Professor of Greek at Yale from 1845 to 1872.

James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, Mukunda Shastri Adkar, and Charles Rockwell Lanman, later serving as a professor at Harvard University from ~1903 to 1934.

James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell College and Yale University under William Dwight Whitney, holding posts at Denison College, Marietta College, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and Brown University.

James Ishmael Ford (born 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sonoma State University, Pacific School of Religion, and under Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant, later founding Boundless Way Zen and the Empty Moon Zen Network.

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned degrees from Northwestern University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under David Tracy, David M. Knipe, Isshi Yamada, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

James L. Fitzgerald (born 1948) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Edwin Gerow and J. A. B. van Buitenen, holding faculty posts at the University of Tennessee and Brown University.

James L. Taylor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Macquarie University by 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide, attested in 2014.
James Legge (1815–1897) was a sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and Highbury College. In 1876, he became a professor at the University of Oxford.

James Luther Adams (1901–1994) worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, where he later held an academic post from ~1956 to 1968.

James Mackintosh (1765–1832) was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and the University of Edinburgh, and he founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, serving as its president from ~1804 to 1811.

James Mallinson (born 1970) is an Indologist educated at Eton, SOAS, and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS and Oxford, becoming Boden Professor of Sanskrit and Director of Graduate Studies at Wolfson College in 2023.

James Mark Shields (born 1971) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was Associate Professor at Bucknell University and an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
